summary: Warren Lee Todd works in philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad and studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007) under Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, having also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami and at Koyasan University. He held positions at Koyasan University, Ryukoku University, Toseiji, and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College.

Watari Yanai (1875–1926) was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1900 to 1903 and held a post there from circa 1919 to 1926.

Wataru Mori (1926–2012) studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1946 to 1951. He held academic posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989), working in philosophy and other fields.
Wataru Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under Minoru Kiyota. Ryose also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, Chandira studied as a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned an MTh and PhD at Harvard University and Harvard Divinity School. He taught at Fordham University (~1969–1972) and Columbia University (~1972–2014).

Wei Lin, a history, archaeology, and Sinology scholar, earned a BA from Nanjing University and a PhD from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Transylvania University, and elsewhere.
Wei Wu is a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the International Buddhist College. In 2026, Wu is attested as an Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015 and joined the faculty of the University of Chicago in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng studied at the University of Chicago and earned a PhD at Harvard under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Teng held positions at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Wei-ming Tu earned a bachelor's at Tunghai University and a PhD at Harvard. He held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard, Harvard-Yenching Institute, and East-West Center, alongside visiting professorships at PKU, NTU, CUHK, and University of Paris.

Weijue Shi (1928–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who was ordained under Linyuan in 1963 and also studied under Lingshuan. He founded Chung Tai Shan, Lin Quan Temple (1987), and the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993).

Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held a teaching post at the University of Hong Kong and was on the faculty at Renmin University of China from circa 2006 to 2017.
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang is a Tibetologist and historian-archaeologist. Huang held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1968–1972). He served as a Professor at the University of Iowa (~1974–2014), where he became Professor Emeritus of Chinese in ~2014.

Wen-ling Jane is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman (attested 2009) and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University, and earned a PhD from Peking University. Mai held a post as visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).
